title: Paul Graham willed Y Combinator into existence
structureWhy: CLIP FIRST. yc-sam-01 opened on b-roll plus synthetic narration and held 32%; clip-only cuts opening on a face held ~63%. This changes that one variable — a human face and a human voice in second one, narration answering rather than introducing.
structureWhy2: clip:0 and clip:1 run back to back and are the SAME sentence with filler removed, so no transition fires between them. Cutting for length must never cost the antecedent: an earlier version opened on 'He himself would cook us dinner', which is a pronoun with nothing to attach to — the viewer never learns who is being described or why it matters.

source.speaker: Sam Altman
source.comment: Passages are in SOURCE time, relative to the extracted a-roll (which starts at 132.0s of the original talk). Cropped 1620x2160 at x=1552 from the 3840x2160 master — crop first, scale last (F14).
source.passagesWhy: 0: 'And my kind of Paul Graham memory is: we would all, every week, come' — NAMES HIM. Without this the whole short is about an unidentified 'he'. 1: skips the 'I think it was on Tuesdays' aside and runs 'he would cook' through to 'the next Google' — the anecdote. 2: the thesis, creating belief out of nothing. The join between 0 and 1 removes filler, not meaning.

publish.title: How Paul Graham Manufactured Startup Optimism
publish.description:
Sam Altman on the Tuesday dinners where Paul Graham convinced eight hopeless startups they were about to take over the world — and why that mattered more than advice.

Commentary and edit: The Next Curve

rights.speaker: Sam Altman

beats.why: lands on the words 'Paul Graham' — names the subject at the moment he is named, so nobody has to guess who 'he' is
beats.caption: PAUL GRAHAM

beats.why: Y Combinator mark on 'eight companies' — the room being described is the first YC batch
beats.whyTint: tint white would flatten the orange field to black then invert it to a solid white square. Only tint marks that are already monochrome.
beats.caption: Y COMBINATOR

beats.why: he would cook / He himself would cook us dinner - literal, and it is the setup of the whole anecdote
we would all walk in feeling very hopeless - the dinner table itself, so the room is seen not just described

voBrollWhy: vo1 order tracks the narration: empty desks on 'most never became Google', skyline on 'Y Combinator did', notebook and deskwork on 'one person decided to act as if it would work', a toast on the 'every Tuesday, over dinner' callback. Strict uniqueness means the dinner shot from the opening cannot return for that callback - the toast carries it instead.
